purpose: Tadalafil is used to treat erectile dysfunction (trouble getting or keeping an erection) in men. It is also used to treat an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH), which can cause difficulty urinating. A higher-dose version is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension, which is high blood pressure in the lungs.
how_it_works: Tadalafil works by relaxing the smooth muscles and widening the blood vessels in certain parts of your body, allowing more blood to flow through. For erectile dysfunction, this increased blood flow to the penis helps you get and maintain an erection when you are sexually aroused. For BPH, it relaxes the muscles in the prostate and bladder to make urination easier.
common_side_effects: Headache, flushing (feeling of warmth or redness in your face), upset stomach, back pain or muscle aches, stuffy or runny nose, and dizziness are the most common side effects. These are usually mild and go away on their own within a day or two.
warnings: Do NOT take tadalafil if you take nitrates (like nitroglycerin for chest pain) — this combination can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Tell your doctor if you have heart problems, low blood pressure, liver or kidney disease, or a history of stroke. If you have an erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism), seek emergency medical care right away as this can cause permanent damage. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol as it can increase side effects like dizziness.
typical_dosing: For erectile dysfunction, the usual dose is 10 mg taken about 30 minutes before sexual activity, and it can work for up to 36 hours. Some people take a lower daily dose of 2.5 to 5 mg every day so they do not have to plan ahead. For BPH, the typical dose is 5 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
